title: ignore: treat dotfiles ending in a dot as hidden
body:
A file whose name starts and ends with a `.`, like `.foo.`, is not treated as hidden. It shows up in `rg --files` without `--hidden`, and so does everything inside a directory with a name like that:

    $ mkdir /tmp/t && cd /tmp/t && touch .a. .b x.
    $ rg --files
    .a.
    x.

`.b` is hidden as expected. With this change only `x.` is listed, and `--hidden` still lists all three.

The cause is `file_name()` in `crates/ignore/src/pathutil.rs`. On Unix it returns `None` for any path whose last byte is `.`. That is meant to cover the `.` and `..` components, but it also matches real names that end in a dot. `is_hidden_path_only` then sees no file name and returns false. The non-Unix version defers to `std` and is not affected.

Now it returns `None` only when the final component is exactly `.` or `..`.

I added unit tests for `file_name` and the hidden check, and a walker test that creates a few of these names and checks the default and `--hidden` results. The walker test fails without the change. It is Unix-only because Windows can't create names that end in a dot. The tests in the `ignore` crate pass.
